title: Error Reporting and Logging
keywords: differences between development and production error handling
subtopics: Differences between development and production error handling.
learning_outcomes: Explain what error reporting and logging contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: error_reporting().
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Failures need an explicit policy. Exceptions should propagate to a layer that can handle them, while logs preserve useful diagnostics without exposing internal details to users. In this lesson, focus on error_reporting(); then compare it with display_errors. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use error reporting and logging when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Failures need an explicit policy. Exceptions should propagate to a layer that can handle them, while logs preserve useful diagnostics without exposing internal details to users. For error reporting and logging, begin with error_reporting(). Also distinguish display_errors; log_errors; application log levels. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

content_blocks.title: A small PHP example for Error Reporting and Logging
content_blocks.code:
<?php
function requirePositive(int $value): int { if ($value <= 0) { throw new InvalidArgumentException("Value must be positive"); } return $value; }
try { echo requirePositive(3) . PHP_EOL; } catch (InvalidArgumentException $error) { echo "Invalid" . PHP_EOL; }

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
